official_statement_rationale: While I recognize that headline CPI inflation at 7.01% is uncomfortably above our upper tolerance limit, I remain concerned about the risks of over-tightening. Monetary policy operates with significant lags, and an aggressive 50 bps hike, when combined with the cumulative impact of recent policy actions, risks inflicting unnecessary damage on a nascent and still-fragile growth recovery. The economy is currently operating with a positive output gap of 0.40%, and while we must anchor inflation expectations, we must also avoid a policy error that sacrifices growth unnecessarily. A 25 bps increase represents a calibrated and prudent path that addresses the inflation challenge while remaining mindful of the need to support economic activity. I therefore vote for a 25 bps increase in the repo rate, while supporting the stance of withdrawal of accommodation.
